title.en: Making a magnet and a compass

text.en:
Kiran stroked a steel needle with a bar magnet fifty times in one direction. Then he laid the needle on a leaf floating in a bowl of water.
The needle slowly turned until it pointed north and south.
"My needle became a compass!" he cheered.

An iron or steel needle can be made into a magnet by stroking it many times in one direction with one pole of a bar magnet. It should be lifted away after each stroke.
A freely hanging or floating magnet always settles in the north-south direction. A needle magnetised this way and floated on a leaf in water makes a simple compass.
A real compass has a magnetised needle on a pivot. It is used by sailors, hikers and pilots to find directions. Keep magnets away from mobile phones and cards and do not drop or heat them because they can lose their magnetism.
A steel needle becomes a magnet when stroked many times in one direction with a bar magnet.
A magnetised needle floating on a leaf turns north-south. This is a simple compass.
A real compass has a needle that spins on a pivot. Sailors and hikers use it.
Do not drop or heat magnets. They can lose their magnetism.

problem.en: Why must we stroke the needle only in one direction?

text.en: Stroking in one direction lines up the tiny magnetic parts inside the needle.
Back and forth strokes would undo the lining up.
So one-direction strokes make a stronger magnet.

prompt.en: A friend says a magnet can be made by only touching a needle once. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: A needle must be stroked many times in the same direction.
One touch gives only a very weak magnet.

points.en: Stroking a needle with a magnet in one direction makes a magnet.
A floating magnet makes a simple compass.
A compass shows north and south.
